subject: Console insights: tenant-aware cost & tail-latency visibility (Acme Health ask)

Subject: Console insights: tenant-aware cost & tail-latency visibility (Acme Health ask)

Folks —

Quick summary: Acme Health's infra/security team asked for an enterprise-level view in the Console that can: 1) attribute token costs to tenant IDs and model variants per-route; 2) surface tail-latency breakdowns (95/99/99.9) by route + tenant; and 3) allow exportable, scheduled reports (CSV/PDF) for monthly audits. They called this out as a hard requirement for procurement to close the deal.

Attached I included a short requirements doc from Acme and a sketch I drew of the UX shape they expect. High-level asks in their language:
- "Per-tenant chargebacks by route and model version"
- "Ability to slice latency tails by customer and route"
- "Audit-ready export and retention controls"

Ask to this group: can product + infra estimate scope and identify roadmap placement + any exceptions we can offer (SLA/capped-cost views vs full per-tenant attribution)? If this needs a separate dedicated project (INF-3421), let's call it out.

Notes: Acme will accept a phased approach if we can commit to a timeline for the first two bullets. They also want RBAC gating so only org-admins see cost breakdowns.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_enterprise_requirements.pdf (PDF), console_route_insights_sketch.png (PNG), infra_cost_snapshot_aug2026.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console insights: tenant-aware cost & tail-latency visibility (Acme Health ask)

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear write-up and attachments. A few immediate questions and trade-offs from a product perspective:

1) Attribution granularity: do we need per-request attribution down to token-level cost, or is per-invoice-period aggregation acceptable? Token-level attribution adds accounting complexity and storage costs.

2) Model variants: are we expected to store model binary tags per-request (adds metadata) or infer from route + deployed model mapping?

3) RBAC and export: RBAC is straightforward if we reuse our existing Console roles, but scheduled exports + retention/encryption requirements become a compliance product ask. Might need Security sign-off.

Operationally I think a staged approach makes sense:
- Phase 1 (MVP): per-route + tenant daily aggregated cost attribution (no token level), latency histograms with 95/99 buckets; CSV export on-demand. Time: ~6-8 weeks.
- Phase 2: scheduled exports, model-variant tagging per-request, UI filters for tail-latency by tenant and model. Time: +6 weeks.

I've created a placeholder ticket: INF-3421 (please @me with any details you'd like included). Can Marissa help prioritize this against the Console backlog? Also looping in Lauren for implications on infra/metrics ingestion.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console insights: tenant-aware cost & tail-latency visibility (Acme Health ask)

Appreciate the framing. A couple of practical notes from PM/UX side:

- UX: The Acme sketch is helpful but they're expecting a single-pane "tenant explorer" that lets them select a tenant and see cost by route, model, and time range with a timeline and tail-latency sparkline. We should avoid cluttering the main Console nav initially — consider a dedicated "Insights" route in the Console nav.

- Telemetry hooks: we'll need consistent tenant IDs surfaced in request metadata (ideally a stable tenant_id header). If infra already emits that, we can rely on metrics; if not, we'll need an ingestion shim.

- Exceptions: for enterprise deals where tenant attribution is a blocker, we could offer a temporary CSV billing export generated from internal tools while Console work proceeds. That could unblock procurement quickly.

Marissa -> I'll prioritize INF-3421 in the next sprint planning and scope a narrow MVP for the first delivery. Markus / Lauren: can you comment on storage and cost implications (estimated GB/day) if we keep 90 days of fine-grained latency traces vs aggregated histograms?

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console insights: tenant-aware cost & tail-latency visibility (Acme Health ask)

Looping infra/observability notes here — quick estimates so we can be realistic with Acme: 

- If we require per-request model variant tagging and keep full request traces for 90 days, expect ~1.8-2.5 TB/month for a midsize customer like Acme (ballpark, depends on traffic and token counts). That drives both storage cost and query latency for ad-hoc slicing.

- A hybrid approach (store aggregated daily cost and 95/99 histograms at fine granularity, plus sample traces for debugging) reduces storage ~6x while enabling the UI features you described.

- RBAC & exports: we can leverage existing auth for viewing; scheduled exports need a small batch worker and storage area (we can reuse the reports bucket). Estimated infra scope: 2 sprints for ingestion + 1 sprint for export worker + 2 sprints for UI.

Action items:
- INF-3421: Karthik/Marissa to confirm MVP fields and acceptance criteria.
- Engineering estimate: Markus to add a short infra-cost breakdown (I've attached a snapshot).
- Sales unblock: Priyom, offer Acme a temporary CSV export (manual) for procurement and commit to delivery milestones in the SOW.

I'll draft a short infra estimate doc tonight and push to the INF ticket.

-Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
